ctx.goal: A skipped red-team result settles: a structured card-only policy skip publishes a head-bound zero-finding result so red-team:clear is set, and every other non-completed outcome never clears but publishes once per head+reason to the needs-you feed.

dismissed.reason: Retry of failed feed publication is required by an earlier independent weakening audit (a failed publish otherwise has no production recovery); poison quarantine was a second audit finding. Kept deliberately, bounded to 25 per call.
Kept: status.head vs job head are separately guaranteed only by this condition.

findings.summary: The live-PR-head fallback in review-job settlement has no named test. The docs promise "stored review head, then prepared lane head, then live PR head from the carry evidence reader", but the tests cover only the first two steps and the all-unavailable 'unknown' case.
findings.failure_scenario: If io.readCarryEvidence(...).headSha were ignored or misread, a skip with no netBasis.rev and no lane head would publish under head 'unknown' instead of the real head. No test would redden. The cost is only a worse needs-you identity, since a fallback head can never clear. I could not mutate the line. A test with readHead null, laneHead absent and readCarryEvidence returning a 40-hex headSha, asserting that settleRedTeamSkip receives that head, would need to redden.
findings.rootCause: The test matrix was built around the stored-head and lane-head paths. The third fallback was added later for identity quality and never got a matching case.
findings.prevention: Add one test for the live-head fallback in review-job-red-team-skip.test.mjs. More broadly, a doc-claim-to-test mapping check for the 'Regression mapping' list in testing.md would catch prose claims that have no test.

findings.summary: The docs claim that admission of a healed card-only skip "retain[s] the seat-row and comment guards". The only admission test asserts that `prior` becomes null. No named test shows that a recorded red-team seat row, or a trusted comment, still refuses a healed fresh admission.
findings.failure_scenario: If a later edit made `redTeamSkipNeedsSettlement` bypass the fresh-mode guards, a head that has both a skipped status and a stale seat row could launch a second model call. The test 'real persisted skip survives drain reads and recovery admission' uses `list: () => []`, so it would stay green. I could not mutate the line to confirm. A test with a recorded seat row alongside a healed-eligible skipped status, expecting a refusal such as `red-team-not-owed`, would need to redden.
findings.rootCause: The heal path is tested at the predicate and the null-prior level. The interaction with the independent guards is asserted only in prose.
findings.prevention: Add an admission test for a healed skip plus a seat row, and one for a healed skip plus a trusted comment.

findings.summary: Settlement-key/pending-record machinery is duplicated and heavy: flushPending (quarantine, mtime rotation, 25-cap) plus a near-duplicate publish-then-mark sequence inside settleRedTeamSkip. The tail of settleRedTeamSkip repeats flushPending's publish/mark/unlink steps instead of reusing one helper.
findings.failure_scenario: A future change to marker/pending semantics (e.g. record schema) must be made in two places; drift makes one path write markers the other does not recognise, causing duplicate or lost needs-you items. Low likelihood, recoverable.
findings.rootCause: Retry was bolted on after the first-attempt path was written, so the publish sequence was copied rather than factored into a shared function.
findings.prevention: Review lens: flag copied multi-step IO sequences; extract a single publishPending(item,key) helper used by both paths.

findings.summary: Docs regression-mapping list is a 30-line prose restatement of test names that will go stale on any test rename; the mapping is not machine-checked. Guarantees do each name a test, so no coverage gap, but upkeep cost is high. Limitation: no tools, mapping unverified by mutation; Risks/Test plan card sections were not supplied.
findings.failure_scenario: A test is renamed; docs point to a nonexistent name and a maintainer wastes time searching. Recoverable friction.
findings.rootCause: Traceability was satisfied by hand-written prose rather than a checked artifact.
findings.prevention: check:standards rule verifying that bold test names cited in docs/agent/testing.md exist in the named test files.

findings.summary: The docs state the settlement head falls back to the live PR head from the existing carry evidence reader (`io.readCarryEvidence`). No test defends that branch, and the regression mapping has no entry for it. The mapping covers read-head precedence and the lane-head fallback, but not the third tier or its error swallowing.
findings.failure_scenario: If the `readCarryEvidence` fallback is removed or broken (wrong field name such as `headSha`, or a thrown error not contained), every existing test still passes. Skips with no read rev and no lane head would then publish as `head: 'unknown'` with per-run identities, so duplicate needs-you items appear instead of one per head. Likelihood is low because this is a rare path; the cost is noisy feed items, not a false clear. I have no tools and could not run a mutation. A test in `review-job-red-team-skip.test.mjs` should fail here: delete netBasis.rev, make `prepareLane` return no head, stub `io.readCarryEvidence` to return `{headSha}`, and assert `settleRedTeamSkip` receives that head. A second case where it throws should assert `head: 'unknown'`.
findings.rootCause: The author wrote the head-fallback chain and the doc sentence together, then wrote tests for the first two tiers. The third tier sits behind a nested try/catch that is hard to reach through the existing fixture, and the mapping list was built from the tests that existed.
findings.prevention: Add a review lens or `check:standards` rule that cross-checks each guarantee sentence in `docs/agent/testing.md` against the regression mapping list. For this case, a test for the live-head fallback and its throwing variant.

findings.summary: docs/agent/testing.md states settlement falls back to "the live PR head from the existing carry evidence reader" (io.readCarryEvidence?.().headSha in review-job.mjs). No test in the diff exercises that third fallback tier. The review-job tests cover only the read head (netBasis.rev) and the prepared lane head. They never supply readCarryEvidence, and none sets both to invalid.
findings.failure_scenario: If io.readCarryEvidence is absent or returns a different shape, the optional chaining swallows it. Settlement then silently publishes under 'unknown', and no test reddens. The doc promises a live-head fallback that nothing defends. I had no tools and could not verify by mutation. The test that should redden is a review-job case with a missing rev, a missing laneHead and a readCarryEvidence stub returning {headSha}, asserting that head is passed to settleRedTeamSkip.
findings.rootCause: The fallback was added as a defensive tier and described in the doc. The regression mapping was written per-guarantee for the first two tiers only.
findings.prevention: Review lens: every tier named in a documented fallback chain needs a named test. A deterministic gate is hard here.

findings.summary: The doc says the mapped test names are "in the files above unless noted". The "Regressions:" line lists only red-team-skip-outcome.test.mjs, review-job-red-team-skip.test.mjs and review-red-team-on-skip.test.mjs. Most mapped names (for example 'colliding 32-bit reason prefixes…', '30 invalid records…', 'flushes at most 25…', 'policy cannot clear an unbound reviewed read') live in red-team-skip-outcome-regressions.test.mjs, which the doc never lists.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer greps the three listed files for a mapped test name and finds nothing. I resolved every mapped name against the diff and each exists, but several only in the unlisted regressions file. The cost is mild friction.
findings.rootCause: The regressions file was split out after the Regressions list was written, and the list was not updated.
findings.prevention: A check:standards rule that every test file touched in a card's changed set is named in the doc section that maps its tests. Otherwise a doc note.

findings.summary: `.converge-state.json`, a local review-tool state file, is added to the repo. It holds an absolute path on the author's machine, review rounds and dismissals.
findings.failure_scenario: The file is committed and merged. It leaks local paths and review-process state into the repo. A later converge run may also read the stale state (round 2, done:false) as its own. This is certain to happen if the file lands, but the cost is small.
findings.rootCause: The converge tool writes its state into the working tree, and the commit step staged everything instead of only the changed files.
findings.prevention: Add `.converge-state.json` to .gitignore, or add a check:standards rule that rejects tool-state files in diffs.

findings.summary: Settlement now runs for every status other than `ran` or `resumed`. That includes deferred outcomes (`deferredByCap`, `deferredByGuard`) and `not-owed`. None of the new tests covers a deferred outcome reaching settlement. The only `not-owed` test checks the stored status string, not settlement. The doc says 'every outcome except ran and resumed' but pins no assertion for deferrals. I could not verify this from the diff alone, and I ran nothing.
findings.failure_scenario: A cap or guard deferral launches no model call. If it is routed through settlement, it publishes a 'red team skipped; not cleared' needs-you item for what is only a transient deferral. That is likely feed noise rather than lost work. Without a test, nothing stops this from changing silently.
findings.rootCause: The settlement condition was written as a negation over the two completed statuses. The enumeration tests cover error/disabled/unknown shapes but not the deferral flags that `summarizeRedTeam` already handles.
findings.prevention: Add a runReviewJob test with `{status:'skipped', deferredByCap:true}` and `{deferredByGuard:true}`. It should assert whether `settleRedTeamSkip` is called and what the finished status result is.

findings.summary: `.converge-state.json`, a review-tooling state file, is added to the diff. It contains an absolute local path (`/Users/nicolasgilbert/workspace/.lanes/...`), the reviewer roster and dismissal reasoning.
findings.failure_scenario: If it merges, the repo carries a developer's local filesystem layout and internal review negotiation state. The file is also churn that later converge runs would overwrite. It does not affect behaviour.
findings.rootCause: The working-tree transport for the converge tool writes its state file inside the lane. It was not gitignored, so it was staged along with the real changes.
findings.prevention: Add `.converge-state.json` to .gitignore, or add a check:standards rule that rejects tool-state files in a diff.

findings.summary: The needs-you feed item's `reason` embeds `redTeam.reason`, which can come from provider or error text. The item is written to disk and published to the feed with no length cap and no control-character stripping. Only the log line is sanitized (`note`).
findings.failure_scenario: A provider error string that contains control characters, newlines or very long text goes into the pending record, the published marker and the feed line unsanitized. This could corrupt feed rendering or bloat the feed. It is a rare path and not exploitable for clearance, because `reason` never grants a clear.
findings.rootCause: Sanitization was added only for the diagnostic log path. The same untrusted string was reused for a persisted and published artifact without applying the same treatment.
findings.prevention: Apply the `note` sanitizer and a length cap to `reason` before it goes into the item. Add a test that a reason with control characters or length over the cap is normalized in the published item.

findings.summary: The documented live-PR-head fallback (readCarryEvidence → headSha, then 'unknown' head) in runReviewJob has no named test. Tests cover read head, prepared lane head, and settleRedTeamSkip with head 'unknown' called directly, but never the job-level path where neither is a real head.
findings.failure_scenario: If the readCarryEvidence branch is broken or deleted, no test fails. Skips with no read or lane head would then publish under 'unknown' instead of the live head, or settlement would throw when the carry reader errors. This is a rare path with a degraded result.
findings.rootCause: The author tested each head source in isolation and the settle function with a forced 'unknown' head, but not the job-level fallback chain that the docs describe in prose.
findings.prevention: Add a review-job test with netBasis.rev absent and prepareLane returning no head. It should assert that a stubbed readCarryEvidence headSha is passed, and that a throwing reader yields head 'unknown'. Not verified by mutation: I have no tools.

findings.summary: createReviewJobIo's production wiring for settleRedTeamSkip is only tested as 'is a function'. The gh pr comment argv, the readComments adapter, and the publishNeedsYou no-op under isUnderTest (a default that silently swallows publication) are never exercised.
findings.failure_scenario: If isUnderTest(process.env) is wrongly true in production, or the gh arguments are malformed, needs-you items are silently dropped and policy clear comments never post. All unit tests stay green because they inject mock IO, so card-only PRs silently never get red-team:clear.
findings.rootCause: Settlement logic was tested through injected IO. The thin production adapter was assumed correct, and the test-mode no-op default is itself unguarded.
findings.prevention: Add a createReviewJobIo test with an injected exec. It should assert the gh argv and body-file input, and assert that publishNeedsYou invokes publishAttention when isUnderTest is false. Not verified by mutation: I have no tools.

findings.summary: A .converge-state.json tooling-state file (round counters, lane paths, a local absolute user path) is included in the diff. It is unrelated to the feature.
findings.failure_scenario: The review-orchestrator scratch state lands in the repo history, leaking a local path and adding noise. It is mildly misleading to later readers.
findings.rootCause: The orchestrator's working-tree transport state was staged along with the feature changes.
findings.prevention: Add .converge-state.json to .gitignore, or add a check:standards rule rejecting it in diffs.

findings.summary: `.converge-state.json` (review-tool state with an absolute local lane path and juror history) is added to the diff as a new file; it is not part of the feature and should not land.
findings.failure_scenario: The tooling artifact merges into main, leaks a local filesystem path, and conflicts or churns on every later converge run (certain if merged; impact is noise only).
findings.rootCause: The converge tool writes its state into the working tree, and the commit staged everything, so the artifact was never filtered out.
findings.prevention: Add `.converge-state.json` to .gitignore, or add a check:standards rule that rejects it in a diff.

findings.summary: The docs state that settlement falls back from the read head, to the lane head, to the live PR head via `io.readCarryEvidence`. The diff has no named test for the live-head fallback, neither the success path nor the case where the reader throws. The tests only cover the read head and lane head. I could not run a mutation (no tools), so a test is named as needed: a review-job test that sets `readCarryEvidence` to return a valid `headSha` with no `netBasis.rev` and no lane head, and asserts `head` equals that SHA, plus a case where the reader throws and `head` is 'unknown'.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression in the live-head branch, such as a wrong property name or a swallowed result, still passes the suite. Settlement then publishes under `unknown` and a new attempt id for every run, so needs-you items are not deduplicated per head. This only happens when both the read head and lane head are absent, which is rare.
findings.rootCause: The fallback chain was extended during review rounds and tests were added for the first two links only. The docs list the third link without a matching test.
findings.prevention: Add a doc-claim-to-test mapping check. Every guarantee line in the docs regression mapping must resolve to an existing test name.

findings.summary: The production wiring in `createReviewJobIo().settleRedTeamSkip` has no behavioural test. This covers the `gh pr comment` post, the `readCompletePrComments` reader, and the `isUnderTest` publisher no-op. The only test is 'exposes the settlement hook' (is a function). The policy-clear path that sets `red-team:clear` is therefore tested only with injected IO. Not verified by mutation (no tools). A test that stubs `exec` and asserts the `gh` argv and body is what should defend it.
findings.failure_scenario: A wrong `gh` argument, such as a bad repo flag or a missing `--body-file`, makes every policy comment fail in production. Policy skips then publish needs-you instead of clearing. All tests stay green. Likelihood is moderate, since the command is a hand-built argv.
findings.rootCause: The tests inject fake IO, which isolates the settlement logic. The adapter that turns it into real `gh` calls was treated as trivial glue and left unpinned.
findings.prevention: Add a test that builds `createReviewJobIo` with a stub `exec` and asserts the `gh` argv, input body, and env.

findings.summary: Docs promise settlement head falls back to the live PR head via the carry evidence reader (io.readCarryEvidence), but no test exercises that branch of runReviewJob. Existing tests cover only the netBasis.rev and prepared-lane-head fallbacks, plus the settle-level 'unknown' head.
findings.failure_scenario: The readCarryEvidence branch is deleted, or its headSha field name is wrong. Any suite stays green, and a skip with no read rev and no lane head is published under head 'unknown' even though a live head existed. The needs-you items then lose per-head dedup and no test reddens. I could not verify by mutation; the test that should defend it is a review-job case with no rev, no lane head, and io.readCarryEvidence returning { headSha }.
findings.rootCause: The author wrote tests for the first two links of the three-step head fallback chain and documented all three. Nothing checks that every documented fallback has a test.
findings.prevention: Add a review-job test that sets io.readCarryEvidence to return a headSha with no rev and no lane head, and asserts the settle call receives that head. A lens check that every fallback named in docs maps to a named test would catch this class.

findings.summary: Docs say healed card-only admission 'retains the seat-row and comment guards' when admission treats a healed skip as fresh (prior set to null). The only admission test asserts prior === null. No test shows a pre-existing red-team seat row or a trusted result comment still refuses a fresh healed dispatch.
findings.failure_scenario: The new `admissionPrior = null` line makes the fresh guard see no prior status. If the guard's row or comment check depended on that status, a healed dispatch could launch a second model call on a head that already has a seat row. The planner-level 'trusted comment' test covers only planRedTeamOnSkip, not job-time admission. I could not verify by mutation; the test that should defend it is a createReviewJobIo admission case with a recorded seat row and policy=true that expects refusal.
findings.rootCause: The author pinned the admission test to the new prior-null output and relied on prose for the unchanged guards. A comment that promises a guard is retained is a test written in the wrong syntax.
findings.prevention: Add a createReviewJobIo admission test with policy=true plus a red-team seat row (or a posted comment) that asserts a refusal such as red-team-not-owed. A review lens could also require a named test for each 'retained' claim.
